hooks.prompt:
You review Japanese prose that the assistant is about to write to a file. Hook input: $ARGUMENTS

The text being written is tool_input.content for Write, tool_input.new_string for Edit, and every tool_input.edits[].new_string for MultiEdit. If that text contains no Japanese prose, respond {"ok": true}.

Otherwise check only the prose; ignore fenced code, inline code, URLs, file paths, and text inside 「」 that is quoted as an example. The goal is text a reader understands in one pass. Flag only clear problems of these kinds:
1. Missing role: a sentence omits its actor or the object of a transitive verb, unless the actor is the assistant itself or the object is named in the same or the previous sentence; or a pronoun or bare count has no referent in the same or the previous sentence.
2. Term collision: a katakana word that is also the name of a Claude Code feature (エージェント, スキル, タスク, フック, プラン, チーム, メモリ, ワークフロー, アーティファクト) is used for the general concept; the fix is a plain Japanese word (作業, 計画).
3. Calque or idiom: an English common noun translated word for word (表面, 着地, 所有, figurative 経路); a name that a product or spec defines for a feature, setting or resource, translated into a common noun instead of kept in its original spelling; or a business idiom or metaphor (筋が良い, 腹落ち, 刺さる, 寄せる, 握る).
4. Padding: a sentence or phrase that can be removed without changing the meaning, or a point stated twice.
When unsure, allow.

If nothing is flagged, respond {"ok": true}. Otherwise respond {"ok": false, "reason": "..."}. Begin the reason with: The file was not written. Rewrite the flagged sentences and retry the same tool call. Then, for each violation, quote the sentence, name the rule number, and state in one sentence what is wrong and which fix the rule calls for. Do not write a rewritten sentence; the assistant rewrites it following ~/.claude/rules/japanese.md.

You review Japanese prose that the assistant is about to post to GitHub with the gh CLI. Hook input: $ARGUMENTS

tool_input.command is a shell command. Respond {"ok": true} without review when any of these holds: the command posts no text to GitHub (for example gh pr view, gh pr diff, gh run list, or gh api without a title, body or comment field); the text is read from a file on disk (--body-file <path>, --notes-file <path>, -F body=@<path>, --input <path>), because .md files are reviewed when written; or the posted text contains no Japanese prose. Text fed on stdin through a heredoc, such as --body-file - <<'EOF', is part of the command and is reviewed.

Otherwise review the posted text: the values of --title, -t, --body, -b, --notes, and title= / body= fields, including text written in a heredoc or $(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF). Check only the prose; ignore fenced code, inline code, URLs, file paths, @mentions, lines quoted from another person (starting with >), and text inside 「」 that is quoted as an example. The goal is text a reader understands in one pass without the conversation that produced it. Flag only clear problems of these kinds:
1. Missing role: a sentence omits its actor or the object of a transitive verb, unless the actor is the assistant itself or the object is named in the same or the previous sentence; or a pronoun or bare count has no referent in the same or the previous sentence.
2. Term collision: a katakana word that is also the name of a Claude Code feature (エージェント, スキル, タスク, フック, プラン, チーム, メモリ, ワークフロー, アーティファクト) is used for the general concept; the fix is a plain Japanese word (作業, 計画).
3. Calque or idiom: an English common noun translated word for word (表面, 着地, 所有, figurative 経路); a name that a product or spec defines for a feature, setting or resource, translated into a common noun instead of kept in its original spelling; or a business idiom or metaphor (筋が良い, 腹落ち, 刺さる, 寄せる, 握る).
4. Padding: a sentence or phrase that can be removed without changing the meaning, or a point stated twice.
When unsure, allow.

If nothing is flagged, respond {"ok": true}. Otherwise respond {"ok": false, "reason": "..."}. Begin the reason with: The command was not run, so nothing was posted to GitHub. Rewrite the flagged sentences and retry the same tool call. Then, for each violation, quote the sentence, name the rule number, and state in one sentence what is wrong and which fix the rule calls for. Do not write a rewritten sentence; the assistant rewrites it following ~/.claude/rules/japanese.md.
